act-one-curtain.title: The parlour has told its story
body: You named the poison, the vessel, the fire and the door -- Sergeant Hollis pins your deductions to the board and looks, for the first time, less like a man doubting and more like a man counting.
Act 2 opens the kitchen and the stairs: where the household moved in the dark, and where a door stood off its bolt for twenty-one minutes.

act-two-curtain.title: The dark half hour has its arithmetic
body: A door off its bolt at half eleven, wet diamond treads crossing the kitchen flags, a wireless singing to nobody at 11:21. The visitor came by the garden, crossed the house without a light, and stood in the parlour while it sat blind.

Act 3 opens the bedrooms, the bathroom and the study: where Peggy's candle burned to the eleven-o'clock mark, where the blotter keeps a pencil's plea, and where a safe holds carbon pages the fire never saw.

act-three-curtain.title: The papers have told their truth
body: A pencil plea under the torch, a cab at 10:19, a candle burned to the eleven mark, and carbons of the confession the fire never saw. The forgeries were Julian's guilt; Peggy's debts were hers alone; the confession was real, and it was going to H.M. before Monday.
Act 4 climbs the attic stair and down the cellar steps: Ruth Marsh's sketchbooks, a candle stub wedged in a door frame, and the truth of a storm-lit night in 1949.

act-four-curtain.title: The attic has said Ruth's name
body: The fox was Ruth Marsh's first, and her last page says it plain: H. carried the light away. A candle stub wedged in the door frame, a stair door bolted from the landing side, an attic key shown to a visitor with Monday's deadline -- the house's oldest silence has a shape now, and it was never an accident.

Every clue from the parlour reads differently tonight: the hay-and-honey ash, the quick certification at 7:20, the pages only one person carried out. Act 5 brings the household to the table -- interrogations, the string board, and the accusation: culprit, method, motive.
